title: Scalar restriction and the sheafified slice-extension adjunction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $U$ an object, and $a:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Give $\mathcal C/U$ its localized topology and put $R_U=R|_U$, $S_U=S|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], scalar restriction $r:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $r_U:\operatorname{Mod}(S_U)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_U)$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and restriction $j_R^*,j_S^*$. For $B=R,S$ let $J_BN=P_N^\#$, where
$$P_N(V)=\bigoplus_{\varphi:V\to U}N(V,\varphi),$$
with the specified summand action and reindexing restriction maps [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Give $J_B\dashv j_B^*$ the adjunction of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], with unit $\eta^B$ and counit $\epsilon^B$.

There is a natural isomorphism $e:rJ_S\xrightarrow{\sim}J_Rr_U$ induced, before abelian sheafification, by the identity on these direct sums and their restriction maps. At $V$, the two $R(V)$-actions on a tuple agree with $(s_\varphi)_\varphi\mapsto(a_V(b)s_\varphi)_\varphi$ for $b\in R(V)$. Under $j_R^*r=r_Uj_S^*$, for every $S_U$-module $N$ and $S$-module $Q$ one has
$$j_R^*(e_N)\circ r_U(\eta_N^S)=\eta_{r_UN}^R,\qquad
\epsilon_{rQ}^R\circ e_{j_S^*Q}=r(\epsilon_Q^S).$$
Here the unit on $(V,\varphi)$ sends a section to its $\varphi$-summand generator followed by sheafification; the counit sends each generator in $Q(V)$ to that same section.

The six functors $r,r_U,J_R,J_S,j_R^*,j_S^*$ are additive and exact. Apply them and $e$ termwise to cochain complexes and strict inverse towers indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. They descend to their unbounded derived categories [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Both displayed identities hold for complexes and derived strict towers with the localized original units and counits, namely the adjunctions of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. Neither flatness of $a$ nor a boundedness assumption is required.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); scalar-action and unit/counit identities extracted from returned parent Steps 1–3.

proof.text: For an $S_U$-module $N$, the underlying abelian presheaves $rP_N$ and $P_{r_UN}$ are identical: both have sections $\bigoplus_{\varphi:V\to U}N(V,\varphi)$. On either presheaf $b\in R(V)$ sends the generator $[\varphi,s]$ to $[\varphi,a_V(b)s]$. Along $t:V'\to V$, either restriction sends $[\varphi,s]$ to $[\varphi t,s|_{V'}]$. The scalar/restriction compatibility is $a_{V'}(b|_{V'})=a_V(b)|_{V'}$. The same identification respects maps $N\to N'$, which act on each generator by the given map. Also $j_R^*r=r_Uj_S^*$, since both evaluate at $(V,\varphi)$ as the same group with action through $a_V$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), summand construction and Hom bijection; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules).

proof.text: Extend the inverse presheaf comparison of Step 1, followed by the S-module sheafification unit, across R-module sheafification using its Hom equivalence. This gives f_N:J_R(r_U N)→r(J_S N). After forgetting module structures its additive map is precisely the abelian sheafification of the inverse presheaf comparison: this follows by applying the abelian sheafification Hom equivalence and naturality of its unit. It is therefore invertible, and the forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. Naturality follows by applying abelian sheafification to the naturality equation of the presheaf comparison. Set e_N=f_N^{-1}. The defining Hom equivalence says f_N carries every R-sheafified generator to its S-sheafified generator; applying its inverse gives the required normalization for e_N. This is the identity-induced comparison, with the same scalar action as in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), summand construction and Hom bijection; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules).

proof.text: Make the Hom bijection of the cited slice adjunction explicit. Write $\sigma_{B,N}:P_N\to J_BN$ for sheafification. An arrow $f:J_BN\to Q$ gives $\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}(s)=f_V(\sigma_{B,N,V}[\varphi,s])$. Conversely a slice-module arrow $\alpha:N\to j_B^*Q$ defines $P_N(V)\to Q(V)$ by $\sum_\varphi[\varphi,s_\varphi]\mapsto\sum_\varphi\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}(s_\varphi)$. Reindexing restrictions and naturality of $\alpha$ make this a presheaf-module arrow; the sheafification universal property extends it uniquely. The two operations are inverse on every summand, hence on the direct sum and then on sheafification. Thus this is the specified construction of $J_B\dashv j_B^*$ in Tag 03DI. The unit (transpose of $1_{J_BN}$) sends $s$ at $(V,\varphi)$ to $\sigma_{B,N,V}[\varphi,s]$. The counit (inverse transpose of $1_{j_B^*Q}$) sends each $[\varphi,s]$ to $s$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), summand construction and Hom bijection; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules).

proof.text: Evaluate the unit equation on a section s∈N(V,φ). By Steps 2 and 3 both sides give the R-sheafified generator [φ,s]. For any two adjunctions the unit equation characterizes a mate: applying the R-adjunction Hom equivalence identifies the inverse mate of the inverse restriction square with e^{-1}. The standard counit identity for this mate, followed by cancellation of e with e^{-1}, gives precisely the counit equation in the statement. This verifies both equations with the fixed adjunctions and the stated orientations.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), summand construction and Hom bijection; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules).

proof.text: The cited restriction/extension lemma gives exactness of $j_R^*,j_S^*,J_R,J_S$. These functors are additive: restrictions act sectionwise, and $P_{f+g}=P_f+P_g$ on each summand implies $J_B(f+g)=J_Bf+J_Bg$ by the unique sheafification factorization. Scalar restriction is additive by definition. It preserves kernels, since the sectionwise kernel subgroup and its induced action do not change. It preserves cokernels too: the sectionwise quotient presheaf is unchanged as an abelian presheaf, and its sheafification has the restricted action by the uniqueness used in Step 2. Kernels and cokernels in module sheaves have precisely these descriptions. Thus $r$ and $r_U$ are exact as well. This uses no flatness of $a$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), summand construction and Hom bijection; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules).

proof.text: Apply each functor to the levels and transition arrows of a strict tower. Functoriality preserves the tower equations; naturality of $e$, $\eta^B$ and $\epsilon^B$ makes their component maps tower morphisms. The tower category is abelian with kernels and cokernels levelwise, so the induced six functors are additive exact by Step 5. The adjunction also lifts levelwise: the natural Hom bijection of Step 3 takes a family of component maps commuting with tower transitions to such a family, and its inverse does the same by naturality. Its unit and counit are consequently the levelwise original ones. Apply the same argument in each cochain degree: naturality makes these maps commute with differentials, the Hom bijection restricts to chain maps, and the equations of Step 4 hold in every degree and level.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), natural Hom bijection, applied componentwise; agent argument for towers and cochain complexes.

proof.text: Use the exact-localization inverse-mate theorem on the inverse restriction square and the adjunctions of Step 3. By Step 4 its ordinary inverse mate is e^{-1}, hence is invertible. The theorem identifies its derived inverse mate with the localization of e^{-1}, conjugated by the specified exact-functor composition isomorphisms. This is the inverse of the derived comparison specified in the statement. The general unit and counit identities for mates now give both derived equations with exactDerivedAdjunction. Repeat this argument in the abelian strict-tower categories using Step 6. Thus the resulting identities are for the localized original units and counits, with no boundedness or flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); exact localization of inverse mates as proved in lem-sf-exact-localization-inverse-mate.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03DI, 03CY, 03DJ: identity presheaf comparison, module sheafification Hom equivalence, and specified slice-adjunction generators. Mate calculus gives the counit and lem-sf-exact-localization-inverse-mate gives the derived identities; tower and cochain identities are componentwise.
